about: The reviewed MCP tool annotations. Each tool's title and four hints are served in tools/list from crates/maidan-mcp/src/tools/catalog.rs, and tool_annotations_contract fails when the two disagree. Each reason names what the handler does; check it against the handler before changing a value.

rules.readOnlyHint: true only when the tool writes nothing: no row, event, claim, read marker, blob or audit row. It equals membership in READ_ONLY_TOOLS (crates/maidan-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs); a tool off that list gets a mutation audit row for every call.
rules.destructiveHint: true when the call deletes or removes a record, revokes authority or access, tombstones, or replaces a value a person or agent stored (a set_* or upsert that overwrites, an edit, a rename, an import that erases), or makes an irreversible state transition. false for additive writes, for toggles of the caller's own view or preference that a sibling tool flips back, and for the claim lease cycle (claim, renew, acknowledge, release). Always false for a read-only tool.
rules.idempotentHint: true when repeating the same call with the same arguments has no further effect on state, including a repeat that is refused and changes nothing. false when each call creates something new, appends an event, or moves a clock forward. Always true for a read-only tool. The per-call audit row is a record of the call, not an effect.
rules.openWorldHint: true when the tool itself reaches outside Maidan's database and artifact store: an HTTP receiver, Slack, GitHub, an embedding provider, a land-gate advisor, or a delivery target the call selects. Background projectors and notifications that mirror an ordinary write because of workspace configuration do not make that write open-world.
rules.name: snake_case of at most 64 characters, the bound Claude and OpenAI clients put on a tool name, and short enough that Claude Code's mcp__maidan__ prefix still fits it. The leading word is a verb that says whether the tool writes: one of read_verbs means read-only and any other means a write, and no name joins two verbs with _or_ or _and_.
rules.mixed: A write whose result the caller then reads as data, not just an echo of the write, so a model could reach for it to look something up. Each one stays a single tool, is never read-only, and its description names the write in the words given here.
